newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville cuts Friday peak prices by $3.00/MWh.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville cuts Friday peak prices by $3.00/MWh.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) cut prices for firm and non-firm power during peak demand hours on Friday by $3.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the agency said Thursday.
BPA continued to offer up to 200 megawatts (MW) of firm power for Friday, but lowered prices to $11.00 per MWh for Northwest deliveries and to $12.00 for California-Oregon border (COB) sales.
Firm off-peak prices were unchanged at $10.50 per MWh for all deliveries.
Up to 500 MW of non-firm power for hours ending 0800-1000 and 1800-2000 PDT was offered at $12.00 (Northwest) and $13.00 (COB), down from $15.00 and $16.00, respectively, for Thursday.
Non-firm power during shoulder hours (1100-1700 and 2100-2200) was offered at $11.25 (Northwest) and $12.25 (COB), down 75 cents from Thursday prices.
Non-firm power during off-peak hours on Friday was offered at $10.50 for all deliveries.
BPA also continued to offer displacement power for hours ending 0100-0600 and 2300-2400 PST at $9.00 per MWh and at $7.00 for Northwest buyers only.
